quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while you ride.
Fit snugly.
Be uncomfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement. This gives you protection and comfort.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply steady pressure to both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the car in front of you as close as possible.
Look only at your controls and not ahead.
Let other drivers know your plans with signals and brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know your plans with signals and brake lights.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane behind a car, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: Wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.
Can cause permanent hearing damage.
Is never dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Exposure to wind noise over time can permanently damage your hearing. Wear earplugs or other hearing protection when you ride.

questions.question: If you drink one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. You should:

options.text: Not wear bright colors during the day.
Wear bright colors during the day.
Wear dark colors during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright colors during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors when you ride to make yourself more noticeable.

questions.question: You drank alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have reduced ability and judgment.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have reduced ability and judgment.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system, and your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the side of the road. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait for it to start moving.
Move to a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you pass an emergency scene.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Motorcycles must have footrests for passengers. Good footing helps prevent your passenger from falling off and taking you with them.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster your body removes it.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after that hour passes.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.

options.text: Following too closely
Honking the horn at the wrong time
Communicating with other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Following too closely
questions.explanation: Following too closely (tailgating) is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance when riding behind another vehicle.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used for quick stops.
Should be used only on slippery roads.
Is weaker than the rear brake.
Is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right
Left
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space possible. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
Air is being released visibly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to move into your lane.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may need to escape if danger arises.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver cannot see you. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce accident chances by:

options.text: Not looking ahead for hazards.
Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.
Making sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, be visible, signal clearly, keep space between you and other vehicles, watch the road ahead, and identify hazards. Always be ready to react to any hazard.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Leave the road.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger and may cause them to tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Riding slowly.
Reading the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter how fast you go. Wearing a good helmet properly greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to ride safely:

options.text: Gets better.
Stays the same.
Gets worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets worse.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride if you have had any alcohol.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work well?

options.text: Fasten securely to your head.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely to your head.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: When there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle can pass on the right if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the other vehicle. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When looking around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for ways to escape danger near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
Check if you can go faster than other vehicles.
Look directly at pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for ways to escape danger near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
Ignore them.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that encourages the tailgater to pass you. Going faster will only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Keep using your mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell drivers about your turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes it hard for other drivers to see your turn signals. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What material gives the best protection in a crash?

options.text: Denim
Leather or synthetic materials
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in a crash. Wear long pants and a jacket while riding.

questions.question: How should you load saddlebags?

options.text: Load them with equal weight on both sides.
Put different amounts of weight in each bag.
Put as much weight as possible in one bag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load them with equal weight on both sides.
questions.explanation: Put about the same weight in each saddlebag. If one bag is much heavier, your motorcycle will lean to one side.

questions.question: How can you reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Look straight ahead of your motorcycle.
Refuse to swerve to avoid danger.
Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds on your path of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds on your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on your path of travel to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react before you reach the danger.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you turn. If you turn too fast, you may slide out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Which surface is potentially slippery?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Gravel roads are slippery. Other slippery surfaces include wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, lane markings, and metal plates.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as effectively as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Immediately take it on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should riders use mirrors?

options.text: All riders should check them frequently.
Only the lead rider should check them.
Riders should not check them often because they are distracting.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check them frequently.
questions.explanation: All riders should check their mirrors often when riding in a group. This helps you watch the riders behind you and keep the group together.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet on a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What should riders know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are nothing to worry about.
Riders should check them often.
They don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders should check them often.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Dark clothes since it is light outside.
Bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even in daylight.
